title: FRM® Certification (Financial Risk Manager)
source: GARP FRM Learning Objectives & Candidate Guide (2024-2026)
summary: The global gold standard in financial risk management, covering Part I risk tools, quantitative analysis, financial markets, and VaR models, and Part II market, credit, operational, liquidity, and investment risk with strict 4-year examination and 5-year experience windows.

standard.name: Standard Professional Risk Pathway
standard.blurb: Pass FRM Part I (100 MCQs, 4 Hours), pass FRM Part II within 4 years (80 MCQs, 4 Hours), and verify 2 years of professional risk experience within 5 years.

stages.title: Stage 1: FRM Part I – Risk Tools & Foundations
stages.subtitle: 4 Modular Curricula (100%) culminating in a 4-Hour Exam (100 MCQs)

nodes.name: Registration & Open Enrollment
nodes.description: Open registration with GARP and enrollment in the FRM program. No collegiate degree or work prerequisites required to sit for the exams.
topics: GARP Enrollment
CBT Scheduling with Pearson VUE
Exam Policy Review

nodes.name: Foundations of Risk Management
nodes.description: Enterprise risk management (ERM), corporate governance, CAPM, APT, Basel regulatory capital framework, historical financial disasters, and GARP Code of Conduct.
topics: Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Frameworks & Governance
CAPM, Multifactor Asset Pricing & Arbitrage Pricing Theory
Basel Regulatory Accord History: Basel I, II, 2.5, and III
Case Studies: Barings, LTCM, Enron, Lehman Brothers, Metallgesellschaft
The GARP Code of Conduct & Fiduciary Ethics

nodes.name: Quantitative Analysis
nodes.description: Probability distributions, statistical hypothesis testing, linear regression, time-series forecasting (AR, MA, GARCH), simulation methods, and copulas.
topics: Probability Distributions: Normal, Lognormal, Student's t, Chi-Square
Hypothesis Testing, Confidence Intervals & OLS Regression Assumptions
Time-Series Analysis: Stationarity, Volatility Clustering, ARCH/GARCH
Monte Carlo Simulation, Bootstrapping & Copula Modeling

nodes.name: Financial Markets and Products
nodes.description: OTC and exchange-traded derivatives, futures, forwards, commodity markets, currency swaps, options strategies, BSM mechanics, and fixed-income debt/MBS.
topics: Mechanics of Futures & Forwards: Arbitrage, Basis Risk, Optimal Hedge Ratio
Foreign Exchange Markets & Cross-Currency Swaps
Options Strategies: Spreads, Straddles, Strangles & Payoffs
Interest Rate Swaps, FRAs & Overnight Index Swaps (OIS)
Fixed Income Securities, Corporate Bonds, MBS & CDOs

nodes.name: Valuation and Risk Models
nodes.description: Value at Risk (VaR), Expected Shortfall, stress testing, option Greeks (Delta, Gamma, Vega), binomial pricing, duration/convexity, and sovereign risk.
topics: Value at Risk (VaR): Parametric, Historical Simulation & Monte Carlo
Expected Shortfall (ES / CVaR) & Coherent Risk Measures
The Option Greeks: Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega, Rho & Dynamic Hedging
Fixed Income Valuation: Modified Duration, Dollar Duration, Convexity
Credit Rating Migrations, Transition Matrices & Sovereign Risk

nodes.name: FRM Part I Examination Sitting
nodes.description: Computer-based examination testing quantitative risk tools, financial markets, and valuation models. Passing score set by GARP standard setting.

stages.title: Stage 2: FRM Part II – Advanced Risk Measurement & Application
stages.subtitle: 6 Modular Curricula (100%) culminating in a 4-Hour Exam (80 MCQs)

nodes.name: Market Risk Measurement & Management
nodes.description: Extreme Value Theory (EVT), volatility smiles, term structure models (Vasicek, Cox-Ingersoll-Ross), correlation risk, and non-parametric VaR enhancements.
topics: Extreme Value Theory (EVT) & Peaks-over-Threshold (POT)
Volatility Smiles, Skews, Implied Volatility & Local Volatility
Term Structure Models: Vasicek, CIR, Ho-Lee, Hull-White
Correlation Risk & Copula Dependency in Stressed Markets

nodes.name: Credit Risk Measurement & Management
nodes.description: Probability of default (Merton model), credit derivatives (CDS), Counterparty Credit Risk (CCR), CVA, DVA, FVA, PFE, netting, and central clearing (CCPs).
topics: Credit Risk Metrics: PD, LGD, EAD, and Expected Loss (EL)
Structural Default Models (Merton) & Reduced-Form Models
Counterparty Credit Risk: CVA, DVA, FVA & Potential Future Exposure (PFE)
ISDA Master Agreements, CSAs, Initial/Variation Margin & CCPs
Credit Default Swaps (CDS) & Securitization

nodes.name: Operational Risk and Resilience
nodes.description: Basel Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA), enterprise risk governance, model risk management, cyber risk resilience, and operational due diligence.
topics: Basel Committee Principles for Sound Operational Risk Management (PSMOR)
Basel Regulatory Capital: Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA)
Model Risk Governance, Model Validation & Backtesting
Cyber Risk, Cloud Infrastructure, Ransomware & TPRM
Business Continuity Planning (BCP) & Operational Resilience

nodes.name: Liquidity and Treasury Risk
nodes.description: Market vs funding liquidity risk, Basel III ratios (LCR, NSFR), asset-liability management (ALM), liquidity stress testing, and funds transfer pricing (FTP).
topics: Liquidity Dimensions: Market Liquidity vs Funding Liquidity
Basel III Liquidity Regulation: Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) & NSFR
Asset-Liability Management (ALM) & Liquidity Stress Testing
Funds Transfer Pricing (FTP) & Collateral Management

nodes.name: Risk Management & Investment Management
nodes.description: Factor investing, portfolio risk budgeting, performance attribution (Brinson-Fachler), hedge fund risk, private equity illiquidity, and pension LDI.
topics: Factor Investing, Smart Beta & Risk-Factor Decomposition
Portfolio VaR Budgeting & Marginal Contribution to Risk (MCR)
Performance Attribution & Appraisal Ratios (Information, Sortino, Treynor)
Hedge Fund Due Diligence & Pension Fund LDI Strategies

nodes.name: Current Issues in Financial Markets
nodes.description: Annually updated research papers: AI/ML in risk modeling, climate risk (NGFS scenarios), digital assets/CBDCs, and banking crises case studies.
topics: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning in Risk & Trading
Climate Risk: Physical/Transition Risks & NGFS Scenarios
Digital Assets, Stablecoins & Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs)
Recent Banking Crises (SVB, Signature Bank, Credit Suisse)

nodes.name: FRM Part II Examination Sitting
nodes.description: Computer-based examination testing advanced market, credit, operational, and liquidity risk. Must be passed within 4 years of passing Part I.
checklists: Must be passed within 4 years of passing Part I
Demonstrate comprehensive scenario analysis across credit, market, and liquidity regimes

stages.title: Stage 3: Professional Experience & Credential Award
stages.subtitle: 24 Months Full-Time Risk Experience + Code of Conduct

nodes.name: 24 Months Full-Time Risk Work Experience
nodes.description: Demonstrate at least two years (24 months) of full-time professional work experience in financial risk management or a closely related role. Must be submitted within 5 years of passing Part II.
topics: 24 Months Professional Risk Experience
Experience Submission Deadline: 5 Years Post-Part II
Qualifying Disciplines: Credit, Market, Operational, Treasury, Audit

nodes.name: Certified FRM Designation Conferred & Ethics
nodes.description: Formal award of the Certified Financial Risk Manager (FRM®) credential and commitment to upholding the GARP Code of Conduct.
topics: Certified FRM Credential Award
GARP Code of Conduct Commitment
Annual CPD Recommended Standard
